main_text.p: hoc observari necesse erat, ut, quot tribus jam exierant, tot fabæ nigræ ex numero noveno detraherentur. Prytanea autem tempus erat dierum xxxv, decima scilicet pars anni Lunaris, quo Athenienses olim in sacrorum & magistratuum ratione plurimum sunt usi, demptis diebus iv, ut placet Sigonio, qui de republicâ Attică, ut dixi, prolixissimè & eruditissimè scripsit: quanquàm ab eo hac in parte magnus Iosephus Scaliger dissentiat, quemadmodum paulò post ostendemus. Præter Prytanes verò, ut vult idem Sigonius ex mente Arpocrationis scriptoris antiqui, itemque Iulii Pollucis, (quanquàm Libanium Sophistam eruditissimum & rerum Atticarum veterum cognoscendarum studiosissimum, aut quisquis is fuit qui alterum argumentum orationi Demosthenis in Androtionem præfixit, quem ego diversum à Libanio fuisse reor, ab illis dissentire fateatur,) alii quoque in senatu præsides tunc erant ex re [illegible, ~6 letters] dicti, numero ix, singuli ex singulis tribubus, quæ in prytaneatu non erant, per prytaneum ἐπιστάτ[?] electi. Epista-ta hic putatur prytanum caput fuisse, ac omnium eorum nomine discutien-da in senatu proposuisse, maximæ in toto senatu autoritatis, & qui annulum

page.notes: The Greek word after "ex re" is too faint to read and is marked illegible. The Greek word "ἐπιστάτ" is a partial reading and is marked [?]. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout; "proposuisse" is read from a worn word and may need checking. Faint garbled marks at the lower right of the scan, beyond the text block, look like show-through or the edge of the facing page and are not transcribed. The paragraph is treated as continuous; no clear indent marks a new paragraph on this page.
